item.title: Putin’s party wins supermajority in Russia’s parliamentary election
item.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin attends a meeting with the head of the Federal Customs Service in Moscow on Sept. 21, 2026. —Vyacheslav Prokofyev—POOL/AFP Russia's electoral commission on Monday said that United Russia, the ruling party aligned with President Vladimir Putin, is projected to win the parliamentary election that has been widely criticized as a “ sham .” The Central Election Commission (CEC) reported that 95% of the votes have been counted after a three-day election that began last Friday and ended Sunday. While the final counts are not expected to be certified until later this week, preliminary figures show that the pro-Kremlin party is projected to win a record 355 seats in the country’s 450-seat Duma, the lower house of parliament, giving United Russia an even larger supermajority than its 2016 record high of 343 seats. item.title: Chancellor vows to stay on for Germany’s ‘democratic future’ after latest loss to far-right AfD
item.description:
Germany's ruling center-right party, Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democratic Union, was shut out of a state parliament for the first time Sunday as the far-right Alternative for Germany scored its second victory this month. Why it matters: The result marks the third state election AfD has won — and its second this month — underscoring its growing strength even as Germany's other major parties refuse to govern with it. Driving the news: Merz, who has low approval ratings, told reporters that "reforms have to come." AfD won about 38% of the vote in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, while the CDU recorded its worst result in any German state election since World War II. The CDU fell from 13% to 4.9% and lost all representation. In Berlin's state election, the Left more than doubled its vote share to 25.7% and finished first for the first time. item.title: British Columbia sues OpenAI and Sam Altman over Tumbler Ridge mass school shooting
item.description:
British Columbia filed a lawsuit against OpenAI over the Tumbler Ridge school shooting, alleging that ChatGPT reinforced the shooter's violent ideation. Paige Taylor White / AFP via Getty Images British Columbia filed a lawsuit against OpenAI over the Tumbler Ridge school shooting. The province alleges ChatGPT reinforced the shooter's violent ideation. The lawsuit seeks recovery costs, including for replacing the demolished school. British Columbia is taking OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman to court over the company's alleged role in a mass shooting that shattered a small Canadian community. item.title: US strikes on alleged drug boats may be ‘crimes against humanity’, UN says
item.description:
Dozens of US attacks on boats in the Pacific and Caribbean have killed more than 230 people since September 2025 A special rapporteur for the UN human rights council has concluded that there are “reasonable grounds to believe” that the United States attacks on boats allegedly carrying drugs in the Pacific and Caribbean “constituted crimes against humanity”. The boat strikes, carried out since September 2025 on the stated grounds of stopping drugs being trafficked by sea to the US, have killed more than 230 people. The latest, on Saturday, killed four people in the Caribbean. Continue reading...

item.title: Carney condemns Yom Kippur shooting outside Canadian synagogue
item.description:
Officials say man was critically injured and officer was wounded in Yom Kippur incident near Belleville synagogue A police officer and a man were wounded in an exchange of gunfire on Sunday near a synagogue in Ontario as members of the Jewish community marked Yom Kippur, authorities said. The man was hospitalized in life-threatening condition. The Canadian province’s special investigations unit said the exchange of gunfire happened near the Sons of Jacob Synagogue in Belleville, Ontario, about 110 miles (160km) east of Toronto. Belleville police said the officer encountered the man at about 7.10pm and that both were taken to a hospital. Continue reading...

item.title: Trump returns to the UN, what will he say?
item.description:
Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin meet at a U.S. airbase on Aug. 15, 2025, in Anchorage, Alaska. Photo by Contributor/Getty Images. After ProPublica reported that a Russian oligarch had financed wedding festivities for Donald Trump Jr., his bride confirmed the facts but not their obvious significance. “It was an extraordinarily generous wedding gift from a friend,” a statement on Bettina Trump’s Instagram said. Dismissing suggestions of any quid pro quo, the statement added: “Generosity doesn’t automatically come with an agenda.” President Donald Trump and his family typically explain their suspicious relations with Russia that way. item.title: UK to refuel Saudi jets to help counter Houthi attacks
item.description:
Andy Burnham seeks stability in Middle East to bring down prices at home as first meeting with Trump looms The UK has agreed to provide defensive air support to Saudi Arabia to help counter Houthi fighters and restore stability in the Middle East while driving down the cost of living at home, Andy Burnham has said, ahead of his first meeting with Donald Trump. The prime minister said he had agreed to a request for air-to-air refuelling of Saudi jets to defend energy infrastructure against the Iran-backed rebels and help keep oil flowing from the Gulf to ease global economic turmoil. item.title: Celia Birtwell ‘humanises’ Burberry in London fashion week closing show
item.description:
Textile designer brings florals, vines and smiley doodles to brand’s luxury checks for one-off paired collection Burberry and Celia Birtwell are both national treasures of sorts. One is Britain’s grandest luxury name, the other the textile designer who dressed bohemian 1960s London in her prints and has a place in art history as David Hockney’s favourite muse. Burberry’s designer, Daniel Lee, has always loved Birtwell’s prints. When the two met this spring, he fell for “her energy, and her zest for life”, and a one-off Burberry meets Birtwell collection that closed London fashion week was born. Continue reading...
